messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High 5xx / gateway timeouts detected for private-inference-gw in VPC-12. Threshold: >20 errors/min. Alerting on-call.

ops-pager: paging devon (eng-sre) - escalation policy: infra->sre-primary.

devon: seeing the alert, jumping in. looking at dashboard now (latency + 5xx).

maya: FYI I was running a security-group audit earlier in that VPC around 08:10 UTC, did not touch NAT or route tables but flagged a stale rule. not applied.

devon: initial checks: private-inference-gw shows sustained 502/504 from downstream services. egress to model-hosting endpoints timing out.

devon: running a quick curl test from one of the GW hosts to external model endpoint...

```
curl -svS https://models-prod.rw.example/models/health -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n'
```

devon: curl times out or returns 502 intermittently (200ms -> 2.8s -> timeout).

eli: I'm oncall-sre, taking handoff. which hosts are failing?

devon: hosts gw-priv-1..gw-priv-6 in subnet a. Errors concentrated on gw-priv-3,4,5. gw-1/2 ok.

eli: checking NAT gateway and conntrack. can you run `sudo conntrack -S` on one of the failing hosts?

devon: pasted output:
```
# conntrack -S
sockets: used 32456
entries: 65530
found: 65530
invalid: 0
recycled: 0
searched: 120450
inserted: 60000
evicted: 470
lost: 0
```

devon: entries looks dangerously high, close to table size (65536).

maya: that explains ephemeral port exhaustion -> new outbound connections start failing and upstream returns 502/504. any recent spike in outbound requests?

devon: logs show traffic burst from batching jobs around 07:58 UTC to model-hosting leading to many short-lived connections (per-host rate spiked ~6x).

eli: nat-gw metrics: SNAT allocation near limit, 90% ephemeral ports used. NAT autoscale didn't kick - health checks showing NAT control plane rate-limit errors.

oncall-sre: tagging customer-impact. devon, maya, eli - please call out which customers on private deployments are affected so we can notify.

devon: customers: AcmeHealth (prod), MailFrame (staging), DeltaDocs (prod). Error rate for AcmeHealth ~38% 5xx on their private endpoint, DeltaDocs ~12% errors.

maya: quick mitigation plan: (1) throttle internal batch jobs to reduce new connections; (2) add temporary iptables SNAT port range expansion on gw hosts; (3) request NAT gateway scale-up from cloud console; (4) roll back any recent egress firewall changes if present.

eli: implementing step 2 now: increasing ephemeral port range and reducing TIME_WAIT on gw-priv-3/4/5. applying sysctl tweaks: 
```
echo 1024 65535 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```

eli: applying on gw-priv-3 (ssh): ok. repeating on 4/5.

devon: throttling batch workers via k8s HPA override and temporarily scaling down concurrent jobs. patch applied to batch-job deployment: replicas -> 2

ops-pager: cloud request submitted to add 3 additional NAT elastic IPs and increase SNAT pool. request id: nat-scale-req-4421.

eli: after sysctl change, conntrack entries dropped from ~65530 -> ~43120 on gw-priv-3. seeing immediate drop in new 5xx.

devon: gw-priv-4 logs show 5xx rate trending down from 35/min -> 6/min.

maya: any possibility a security group rule was changed to force traffic through a different NAT path? I checked Audit Logs earlier, no egress SG changes at 08:00-08:30.

eli: double-checked route tables and peering: no recent route table modifications. peering status healthy.

devon: still seeing some residual 504s for a small subset of requests - likely in-flight connections dropped while conntrack evaporated.

oncall-sre: customer impact summary so far: AcmeHealth: ~38% errors (partial outage for inference), DeltaDocs: ~12% elevated errors (degraded), MailFrame: staging, low impact. Impact window started ~07:58 UTC, mitigations began ~08:14 UTC.

maya: sending external comms draft to PS and CSMs for AcmeHealth. will wait for final confirmation before sending.

eli: NAT scale request approved. Cloud console shows additional EIPs attached and SNAT pool increased at 08:28 UTC.

devon: 5xx rates across private-inference-gw now down to baseline (~1-2/min). specifically for AcmeHealth dropped from 38% to 1.8% over 12 minutes.

ops-pager: incident-bot: marking incident as mitigated (partial mitigation completed). Recommend creating follow-up action items: increase conntrack limit, add autoscale trigger for NAT when conntrack > 70%, add alert for ephemeral port depletion, run retro.

eli: temporary sysctl change was applied to hosts and will be made persistent via image bake and config repo change. I'll open a PR to infra-config: infra/config#2046.

devon: handoff to eli for post-incident cleanup and postmortem. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline.

maya: noted. taking PS notification step after final metrics stable for 30m.

eli: initial root cause hypothesis: ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT path due to sudden batch job spike + NAT control-plane request rate limiting prevented timely autoscale. No firewall/SG changes found.

oncall-sre: recording participants and next steps. ETA for retro doc: EOD. tagging owners: eli (postmortem writeup), maya (customer comms), devon (timeline + metrics).

devon: closing loop - if anyone sees recurrence, re-open and page. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
